blocks.text: 8. The Standard of Frugality and Excess

inline.s: To be frugal with oneself while being able to give to others is foremost; not to be dissolute amid wealth and honor, and for women not to vie for showy adornment, doubles the merit.
In a single day, in food and clothing, delight in simplicity and treasure one’s blessings, and practice giving and relief. The poor toil contentedly, neither complaining nor coveting.
each, one merit

For fifteen days, refrain from cooking and killing, restrain cravings and desires; men to their work and women to theirs, not wasting food and clothing. Cause one person to give up extravagance and indulgence; one household to be frugal and simple and generous in giving.
each, ten merits

blocks.text: 9. The Standard of Disposition and Conduct

inline.s: To transform one’s temperament by bearing loss and enduring insult is foremost; one should at all times make progress and correct one’s faults.
[Temperament] the constitution of one’s psychology and character.

In a single day, respect the aged and cherish the young, love one’s peers, endure insult and accept toil, treat noble and base alike, repay kindness and resolve enmity. Hear disagreeable words. Receive one discourtesy without anger. Suffer one slander without contesting it
each, one merit
For fifteen days untiringly, transform one shortcoming of temperament. Endure a great wrong that is hard to bear.
each, ten merits
With no temper rising, rejoice everywhere and transform others everywhere.
one hundred merits

Arrogance and contemptuous mockery. Rash and sharp jesting. Harsh speech and curses. Making a nickname for someone. Fabricating songs and ditties. Double-tongued slander to set people at odds. Breaking a promise. Claiming another’s accomplishment.
Consider the size of the matter; for the great ones the fault is tenfold.
Empty words to win favor
(telling lies to please)
. Women fond of idle roaming. Much talk and foul abuse.
each, one demerit
Delighting in talk about women. Bullying the weak and deceiving the simple. Scheming secretly
(using treachery and secret plots)
. Fabricating slander to frame a person. Destroying another’s success.
all, ten demerits
Ever practicing lawsuits and quarrels to put others to shame. Using sorcery to harm people. Setting the mind to injure others. A woman dominating and bewitching her husband.
all, one hundred demerits
[Double tongue] stirring up right and wrong and sowing discord.

blocks.text: 10. The Standard of Reverence for the Sages

inline.s: To be frequently grateful, to praise, and to emulate [the sages] is foremost.
Profaning the scriptures. Soiling printed paper with filth. Excreting
(urine and feces)
and spitting without regard for the three lights
(sun, moon, and stars)
. When praying for blessings and warding off calamities, not cultivating good deeds but making wicked vows to sacrifice livestock. Women fond of entering temples.
each, one demerit
Mocking, ridiculing, and slandering sages and worthies. Neglecting one’s ancestors
each, ten demerits
Striking and cursing the gods. Defiling and desecrating Buddhist temples. Preaching apostasy against the sages.
all, one hundred demerits

blocks.text: 11. The Standard of Keeping the Mind

inline.s: In a single day, in word and deed wholly good, keeping the mind set on bestowing relief upon the whole world and guiding the people.
one merit
Sharing goodness with others; reforming faults so as to become new each day, until fifteen days.
ten merits
With no private thought appearing, few thoughts and dreams at rest, kindness ever more sincere, until one month.
one hundred merits
Being always thus, compassion
(earnestness)
natural, dwelling in emptiness with perfect response
(with the mind attached to nothing, responding to all with fullness)
merits without measure
Lustful thoughts, greedy thoughts, malicious thoughts, envious thoughts, and fawning worldly thoughts, turning over and over without being removed.
one demerit
Wicked thoughts rolling on for several days and taking shape in action
ten demerits
